result.summary:
I searched the web and read the full text or abstracts of the key works: BCCP in both the arXiv and Political Analysis versions, the pintervals paper (arXiv 2601.03994), Wang et al. 2023 (BFQR, full text), Sadinle, Lei and Wasserman 2019 (full text), Kandinsky CP, Izbicki et al. 2020, Yi et al. 2025, and the 2025-2026 preprints on response bins, label shift, tail-specific intervals and long-tailed conformal classification. I found no paper or package that already proposes conditional-density level sets with stratum-specific thresholds for a continuous outcome, or proves their size-optimality. The method and its framing therefore survive. Compared with cycle 1, the positioning is now mostly honest: Mondrian/BCCP validity is not claimed, Proposition 2 is credited as the per-stratum form of known level-set results, Kiyani, Barber et al. 2023 and Podkopaev & Ramdas are cited, the floor rule is disclaimed, and the gain over S-NCP is stated to be small.

Several credit and attribution errors remain. A hostile reviewer, especially one of the BCCP or BFQR authors, would catch them, and some are factual misstatements about other people's papers:
(1) Proposition 3 is presented as a new proof, but Sadinle et al. (2019, Theorems 14 and 16) already prove, with rates, that a plug-in classifier calibrated by split conformal within each class converges to the class-specific oracle. Sadinle et al. also characterise the null region (empty sets) of the class-specific oracle and give remedies; this was requested in cycle 1 and has still not been done.
(2) The manuscript says twice that Randahl et al. note the BCCP guarantee holds for any score. The published BCCP article does not say this. The source is the pintervals paper and package, which also offer heteroscedastic and custom scores for BCCP. That paper is not cited, and the abstract and highlights still compare against an unqualified "bin-conditional conformal prediction" (cycle-1 C1-02 items 1 and 3, inadequately fixed).
(3) Wang et al. 2023 predates BCCP and already evaluates an equal-level, Y-binned label-conditional CQR baseline (LCQR), which is the paper's S-CQR. The related-work paragraph on BFQR introduces the method twice and misdescribes Wang et al.'s Fig. 1. Wang et al.'s Theorem 3.1 (equalized versus outcome-conditional coverage) is not credited in Section 3.2.
(4) The directly analogous classification literature on long-tailed conformal prediction is missing: Ding, Fermanian & Salmon (ICLR 2026); Liu, Huang & Ong (AAAI 2026); Bhattacharyya, Ding & Barber (arXiv 2606.28598, which characterises the smallest sets under weighted class-group coverage). It is relevant to the motivation, to Proposition 2 and to the floor variant.
(5) The highlights and abstract overstate what is new and what was found: "guarantees coverage of rare, extreme outcomes" although top-1% coverage is 0.736, and "smallest ... on 31 datasets".

None of these issues needs a new experiment. All can be fixed in the text within a day. Once they are fixed, I consider the novelty positioning ready for ESWA submission. The realistic residual risk is an editor judging the methodological increment over BCCP plus S-NCP as modest; the paper already discloses this.

issues.title: Proposition 3 (asymptotic size-optimality of the plug-in procedure) is the continuous-outcome counterpart of Sadinle et al. (2019) Theorems 14 and 16, which are not credited
issues.evidence: manuscript_filled.md line 24 (contribution 1): "We prove that their plug-in conformal version is asymptotically size-optimal under uniform consistency of the density estimate (Proposition 3)." Line 140: "its proof (Appendix A) follows the plug-in arguments of @lei2013distribution and @izbicki2022cdsplit". The abstract (line 8) also says "We show ... that their plug-in conformal version is asymptotically optimal". Sadinle, Lei & Wasserman (JASA 2019; arXiv 1609.00451v2, Section 4) cover exactly the class-specific (label-conditional) case. Their Theorem 14 gives a rate bound P_y(Ĉ_y Δ C*_y) ≤ c(γ_n + sqrt(log n / n)) for the plug-in class-specific classifier under sup-norm consistency of p̂ and a margin condition at t_y. Their Theorem 16 states that the same result holds for the split-conformal version, which calibrates thresholds within each class (their Eq. 7, "label validity" in Vovk's terms). Proposition 3 is this result with Lebesgue measure in place of counting measure. It is weaker, since it gives no rate. src/02_theory.md line 58 credits only the marginal level-set results. The manuscript cites Sadinle only for the oracle characterisation (Proposition 2).
issues.corrective_action: In 02_theory.md line 58 (before Proposition 3), add: "For classification with class-specific coverage, @sadinle2019least [Thms 14 and 16] prove the corresponding consistency, with rates, for the split-conformal plug-in classifier calibrated within each class; Proposition 3 is its counterpart for a continuous outcome and fixed strata, stated without rates." In 01_intro.md line 11, replace "We prove that their plug-in conformal version is asymptotically size-optimal" with "We show, following the class-specific results of @sadinle2019least, that their plug-in conformal version is asymptotically size-optimal". Change "We show" in the abstract to "We extend known level-set results to show" (or similar). Add the same credit to the cover-letter contribution 1 and to the Section 8 sentence "their plug-in conformal version is asymptotically optimal".

issues.title: BCCP misattributed and under-described: the published BCCP article never states validity 'for any score'; the score-agnostic reference implementation (pintervals) is not cited; the headline comparator is still unqualified
issues.evidence: src/01_intro.md line 9, src/015_related.md line 21 and src/02_theory.md line 33 (manuscript_filled.md lines 52 and 115) state that "@randahl2026bin note that it holds for any score" / "note that the bin-wise guarantee holds for any score". I checked the Political Analysis 34(1):96-108 full text (Cambridge core reader) and arXiv 2410.14507v2. BCCP's guarantee is stated for its algorithm with the absolute prediction error. The phrase 'any measure of dissimilarity' appears only in the generic split-conformal background, and no score other than the absolute error is discussed. The score-agnostic statement is in the pintervals paper (Randahl, Hjort & Williams, arXiv 2601.03994, Jan 2026, Section 2.1 and the pinterval_bccp description). That paper says pinterval_bccp takes the same score options as pinterval_conformal: absolute (default), relative, zero-adjusted relative, heterogeneous and raw errors, or a user-supplied custom score. It also says both union and contiguized forms 'achieve at least the desired coverage level'. The bib already contains randahl2026pintervals (CRAN, line 1361), but no manuscript source cites it (grep of manuscript/src returns nothing). So BCCP's own implementation already supports a heteroscedastic, S-NCP-like score and could take the density score as a custom function. The abstract (line 8), however, says "smaller than bin-conditional conformal prediction on 24 of 31 datasets", and highlight 4 / Section 7.1 speak of BCCP without naming the score. Cycle-1 C1-02 asked to "Rename ... 'BCCP with the absolute-residual score'" and to "Describe BCCP accurately ... score-agnostic, with heteroscedastic scores in its reference implementation". Response_01 C1-02 does not report doing either. The fix is inadequate.
issues.corrective_action: (a) Delete "@randahl2026bin note that it holds for any score" in all three places. Replace with: "the guarantee holds for any score (it is the Mondrian argument), and the reference implementation of BCCP [@randahl2026pintervals; Randahl, Hjort & Williams, arXiv:2601.03994] accepts absolute, relative, heterogeneous and user-supplied scores". Add the arXiv paper to the bib. (b) In Section 2.2 / 5.4, say that BCCP with pintervals' heterogeneous score is close in spirit to S-NCP, and that SDLC can be viewed as BCCP with a particular custom score. The contribution is the choice and theory of that score, not a new calibration rule. (c) In the abstract, write "smaller than bin-conditional conformal prediction with the absolute-residual score (BCCP) on 24 of 31 datasets". Use the same qualifier in highlight 4, Section 7.1 and the cover letter, as already done in Section 8.

issues.title: Wang et al. (2023) credited inaccurately: priority, the existing equal-level Y-binned CQR baseline (LCQR = S-CQR), a duplicated BFQR introduction, a misdescribed figure, and their Theorem 3.1
issues.evidence: (i) Priority. src/01_intro.md line 9: "@randahl2026bin proposed it as bin-conditional conformal prediction (BCCP)". Wang et al. (NeurIPS 2023, arXiv 2311.02243, Nov 2023) calibrate within Y-bins one year before BCCP (arXiv 2410.14507, Oct 2024). They also describe their method as "a variant of Mondrian conformal prediction" (Sec. 4.2). (ii) LCQR. Wang et al. Sec. 5.1 compares against "Label-conditional Conformalized Quantile Regression (LCQR) ... designed for classification ... We adapt it to regression tasks". Sec. 5.2.2 explains its width: "enforcing all bins to reach the same high coverage rates generates prediction results with little useful information". That is Y-binned CQR at a common level, i.e. the S-CQR baseline here. manuscript_filled.md line 15 of Section 5.4 says only that S-CQR "is related to the binned calibration of @wang2023equal but omits its level optimisation". (iii) Duplication. manuscript_filled.md line 50 introduces BFQR twice: "their binned fair quantile regression (BFQR) splits $Y$ into equal-mass bins ..." and two sentences later "Their binned fair quantile regression (BFQR) forms equal-mass bins ..." (src/015_related.md line 19). (iv) Fig. 1. The same paragraph says Wang et al. "illustrate that standard methods mis-cover the head and tail bins of the outcome". Their Fig. 1 shows coverage differences between gender groups within the head and tail salary bins under equalized coverage, not overall mis-coverage of those bins. (v) Theorem 3.1. Wang et al.'s Theorem 3.1 (Mutual Exclusivity) shows that coverage equalised across X-defined groups and coverage equalised conditionally on Y cannot both hold when A and V depend on Y. Section 3 of their paper states that equalized coverage "fails to ensure equal coverage conditional on Y, especially for extreme values of Y". This is the qualitative statement of manuscript Section 3.2 ("Covariate-conditional validity does not imply target-conditional validity"), but Section 3.2 cites Wang et al. only for empirical under-coverage (line 89).
issues.corrective_action: (i) In 01_intro.md line 9, write: "@wang2023equal calibrate within bins of the outcome to equalise coverage across groups, and @randahl2026bin proposed bin-conditional conformal prediction (BCCP) for the skewed distribution of conflict fatalities." (ii) In Section 5.4, add: "S-CQR with a common level coincides with the label-conditional CQR (LCQR) baseline of @wang2023equal, who report it to be wide." (iii) Merge the two BFQR sentences in 015_related.md line 19 into one description. (iv) Replace the Fig. 1 description with: "and they show that equalized coverage leaves coverage unequal across groups within the head and tail bins of the outcome". (v) In Section 3.2 after Proposition 1, add: "@wang2023equal [Thm 3.1] show that equal coverage across covariate-defined groups and equal coverage conditional on $Y$ are mutually exclusive; Proposition 1 quantifies the analogous gap for the oracle covariate-conditional set."

issues.title: Missing the directly analogous literature on conformal prediction for long-tailed (imbalanced) classification, including recent optimal-set results under class-group coverage and threshold interpolation
issues.evidence:
The manuscript positions itself as the regression counterpart of label-conditional coverage (lines 46, 77). It does not cite the 2025-2026 work on conformal prediction for long-tailed classification, which addresses the same problem (marginal sets under-cover rare labels) for discrete labels:
- Ding, Fermanian & Salmon, 'Conformal prediction for long-tailed classification' (ICLR 2026; arXiv 2507.06867). It introduces macro-coverage, an approximately optimal 'prevalence-adjusted softmax' score, and a procedure that linearly interpolates between marginal and class-conditional conformal thresholds.
- Liu, Huang & Ong, 'Conformal prediction meets long-tail classification' (AAAI 2026, vol. 40, pp. 23828-23836; arXiv 2508.11345).
- Bhattacharyya, Ding & Barber, 'Conformal prediction with macro-coverage guarantees' (arXiv 2606.28598, June 2026). It gives finite-sample guarantees for weighted averages of group-conditional coverages over label groupings and 'characterize[s] the form of the smallest prediction sets' with a matching score, connected explicitly to Sadinle et al.
The grep of references_verified.bib finds none of these. They matter for three passages:
(a) The motivation (line 20) and Section 2.3 claim (line 58) that guarantees for rare targets 'have so far come from conflict forecasting and fair regression'.
(b) Proposition 2, whose classification analogues now include weighted label-group objectives.
(c) The floor variant (line 182). Threshold interpolation between marginal and class-conditional calibration is a published compromise, and the floor rule credits only @wang2023equal and @kiyani2024length.
issues.corrective_action: Add two or three sentences to Section 2.2 (classification paragraph, src/015_related.md line 15): "In long-tailed classification, marginal sets under-cover rare classes in the same way [Ding, Fermanian & Salmon 2026; Liu, Huang & Ong 2026]; proposed remedies interpolate between marginal and class-conditional thresholds or target macro-coverage, the unweighted average of class-conditional coverages, for which the smallest sets and a matching score have been characterised [Bhattacharyya, Ding & Barber 2026]." In Section 4.5, add Ding et al. (threshold interpolation) as a principled alternative to the floor rule. In Section 7.3, name macro-coverage over strata, with the score $f(y|x)/f_Y(y)$ suggested by those results, as an untested intermediate guarantee. Verify all three entries on DBLP, the AAAI proceedings and arXiv before adding them to references_verified.bib.

issues.title: Empty sets and the 'coverage reallocation' remark do not credit Sadinle et al.'s null-region analysis (cycle-1 C1-04 item 5 not implemented)
issues.evidence: manuscript_filled.md line 152 derives that the oracle set "is empty whenever $t_k\sigma(x)>\max g$" and reports that SDLC returns empty sets for 0.36% of test points (line 140; Table 2 'Empty %' 0.36 vs S-NCP 0.07). Sadinle et al. (2019, Sec. 2.2 after Theorem 6, and Sec. 3) show that the class-specific level-set oracle has a 'null region' {x: H(x)=∅}. They give a sufficient condition for its absence (Σ_y t_y ≤ 1) and propose two principled remedies, including 'accretive completion' (Algorithm 1), which also applies to the split-conformal estimator. Cycle-1 review C1-04 item 5 asked to "Discuss Sadinle et al.'s null-region remedies". The response_01 entry for C1-04 does not mention it, and grep for 'null region|accretive' in manuscript/src returns nothing.
issues.corrective_action: In Section 4.2 ('Coverage is reallocated across inputs'), add: "Empty sets are the regression counterpart of the null region of class-specific level sets [@sadinle2019least, Sec. 3], who show that it is generic and propose filling it (accretive completion) at a controlled cost in size." In Section 7.2 item 3 or the limitations, name a simple remedy that keeps validity: return the hull of the stratum pieces closest to $\hat\mu(x)$, or $[\hat\mu(x)\pm\epsilon]$, for empty sets. Adding points never lowers coverage, so this preserves (5). An optional evaluation from cache is not required.

issues.title: Highlights and abstract overstate novelty and results
issues.evidence:
src/highlights.md:
- Line 4: "Calibrating within target strata guarantees coverage of rare, extreme outcomes." Two problems. The device is established Mondrian/BCCP calibration, and the paper explicitly does not claim it (lines 22, 52). And the guarantee does not extend to extreme outcomes beyond the calibrated strata: SDLC covers 0.736 of the top 1% (Table 2), and line 73 says "its coverage remains below the nominal level for every method".
- Line 5: "Stratum-wise density level sets are the smallest stratum-valid prediction sets" reads as a new result. It is the per-stratum form of Sadinle et al. Theorem 6 (see line 46).
- Line 6: "SDLC gave the smallest stratum-valid sets on 31 datasets, confirmed on 17" reads as smallest on each dataset. In fact SDLC is larger than S-NCP on 4 CTR23 datasets (line 271), and the S-NCP and S-HPD geometric-mean CIs include 1 on the held-out data (Table 7: 0.977 [0.940, 1.028], 0.984 [0.963, 1.014]).
- Abstract line 8: "We show that conditional-density level sets ... are the smallest stratum-valid sets" gives no hint that this extends known classification results.
issues.corrective_action:
Rewrite the highlights, each ≤ 85 characters. Suggested wording:
(2) "Stratified (Mondrian) calibration restores coverage in every target stratum"
(3) "Size-optimal stratum-valid sets are density level sets with per-stratum thresholds"
(4) "SDLC gave the smallest stratified sets on average; replicated on 17 held-out sets"
In the abstract, use "Extending level-set results for class-specific coverage, we show ...". Optionally add "with the absolute-residual score" after "bin-conditional conformal prediction" (see the BCCP issue).

issues.title: Contribution 2 claims an 'exact, stratum-exact implementation' with linear cost, but the reported geometry is that of an interpolant, and linear cost is not distinctive
issues.evidence: src/01_intro.md line 12 (manuscript_filled.md line 25): "It has an exact, stratum-exact implementation whose cost is linear in the number of test points." Section 4.4 (line 174) says that size, pieces, hull and alerts are computed numerically: "The reported geometry is therefore that of the stratum-exact set for the piecewise-linear interpolant of $\hat g$." Only coverage membership is exact. Grid error is up to 0.2% in mean size and 1.5% per point (Table S4). Every split-conformal method has cost linear in the number of test points. The cover letter (contribution 2) repeats the claim.
issues.corrective_action: Replace with: "Coverage is evaluated exactly at the observed target, and set geometry is computed stratum-exactly for a piecewise-linear interpolant of the noise density (grid error ≤ 0.2% in mean size), at O(G log K) per test point." Apply the same wording in the cover letter. Do not present linear cost as a contribution.

issues.title: The dedicated tail-alert baseline (TC-LS/TC-H) and the label-shift literature lack standard credits
issues.evidence: Section 5.4 (manuscript_filled.md line 19, src/03_setup.md line 34) introduces the "class-conditional conformal tail classifier" without a citation, and Section 2.3 (line 58) also describes it uncited. It is split-conformal label-conditional calibration of a binary event, i.e. Neyman–Pearson classification with the miss rate controlled by an order statistic of the positives' scores (Lei 2014, Biometrika, 'Classification with confidence', already in the bib as lei2014classification; Sadinle et al. 2019; Tong, Feng & Li 2018, Science Advances 4:eaao1659, the NP umbrella algorithm). Section 2.4 lists regression label-shift methods (yi2025, lee2026split). It omits the recent preprints by Choi (arXiv 2607.02173 and 2609.27976, 2026) on conformal prediction under continuous label shift in regression. The latter shows that exact validity under continuous exponential tilts makes sets unbounded. That directly supports the paper's point (Corollary 1, Table 8) that stratified calibration is exact only for whole-stratum re-weighting.
issues.corrective_action: In Section 5.4, add "[cf. @lei2014classification; @sadinle2019least; Tong et al. 2018]" after "class-conditional conformal tail classifier". Optionally, add one sentence in Section 2.4: "Exact validity under continuous tilts of the target is generally attainable only with unbounded sets [Choi 2026], which is consistent with Corollary 1(ii)-(iii)." Verify each entry before adding it to the bib.
